newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm amid crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm amid crude gains.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were expected to end steady to firm on Wednesday as supplies were deemed adequate to meet demand amid a firm crude market, traders said.
But prices were expected to soften by late October when more MidEast cargoes arrive in the region, they said.

An offer was seen from a major for mid-October loading supplies at $119 a tonne, a dollar over Tuesday's quote of $118. Some traders said prices may move higher on crude gains and higher paper quotes.
October paper, was bid/asked at $117.25/118.00, higher from Tuesday's at $115.50/$116.
But bids from China were scarce, said a trader.
Traders were expecting at least two cargoes from Kuwait, one from Venezuala, and the normal exports from Iran in October.
They said as China has been covering its requirements from South Korea and Japan, the MidEast cargoes would place a downward pressure on Singapore prices in late October.
A South Korean refiner told Reuters he has no supplies in October while a Japanese trader said he might have a cargo of fuel oil from its processing contract in Okinawa.
